title: Zelary
full_review:
In the World War II period drama "Zelary" (Sony Classics), Ana Geislerova plays Eliska, a cosmopolitan medical student involved in the Resistance movement during the Nazi occupation of Czechoslovakia.

When her safety is threatened by the Gestapo, Eliska is forced into hiding in the eponymous mountain village where she takes an assumed name -- Hanna -- and marries (for appearances) a goodhearted but unrefined peasant (Gyorgy Cserhalmi). Earlier, she had saved his life by donating blood for an emergency transfusion.

Sharing little else in common than her platelets, their unlikely bond slowly warms into friendship and eventually romance. But Hanna cannot escape the gathering storm clouds of history which cast ominous shadows over her newfound happiness.

Directed by Ondrej Trojan and inspired by actual events, the old-fashioned tale of wartime romance weaves timeless themes into a poignant tapestry full of humanity and pathos.

"Zelary" eloquently captures the visual poetry and rustic rhythms of love, life and death among people at one with the land, its stunning photography revealing nature in all its beauty and cruelty.

Some of the scenes are difficult to watch -- especially a brutal attempted rape and a series of wartime atrocities -- but the film's overall message is uplifting. The movie's positive depiction of the local priest and the villagers' devotional life is particularly refreshing, though a comment by a small peasant child could be construed as mildly irreverent.

Brilliantly crafted and buttressed with stellar performances and rapturous vistas of the Moravian mountains, "Zelary" is a hopeful celebration of simple values, community and the nobility of the human spirit.

Subtitles.

Due to recurring violence, including an execution and several rapes, as well as sexual situations with nudity, the USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is L -- limited adult audience, films whose problematic content many adults would find troubling. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted.
